chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ceased the Talbiyya when the sun declined on the Day of Arafah, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to cease the Talbiyya when the sun declined on the Day of Arafah.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: So when you cease the Talbiyya, then upon you is the Tahleel, the Tahmid, the Tamjeed, and the Thana' upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.التَّحْمِيدِ: Tahmid, the recitation of 'Alhamdulillah' (All praise is due to Allah).
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The Talbiyya, the specific declaration of response to God's call during Hajj (Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk).
key_terms.التَّمْجِيدِ: Tamjeed, the glorification of Allah (often associated with 'Subhanallah').
key_terms.التَّهْلِيلِ: Tahleel, the recitation of 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah).
key_terms.الثَّنَاءِ: Thana', praise and eulogy of Allah's attributes.
key_terms.زَاغَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun declined (reached its zenith and began to move west), marking the time for Dhuhr prayer.

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyya during Hajj and what should they recite instead?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise moment for terminating the Talbiyya at Zawal of the sun on the Day of Arafah, a practice consistently observed by the Prophet and Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin). It transitions the pilgrim from the declaration of arrival to a state of continuous glorification (Tahleel, Tahmid, etc.), reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' ritual precision. This shift marks the spiritual climax of the Hajj, where the pilgrim stands in humble servitude before Allah at the Mount of Mercy.
